children: Gold falls in early Asian trade. Investors are focusing on Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's remarks at the International Monetary Fund meeting in Bangkok, Infinox's Thadeu Dos Santos says in a note. A hawkish message could partly reverse the recent bond rally and add renewed pressure on gold. On the other hand, a more patient stance could allow yields to remain lower and support gold's recovery, he says. Spot gold is down 0.3% at $4,156.73 an ounce.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)
